items.behaviour: Picking an interface scale draws the whole canvas -- 3D scene included -- larger
items.defect: The row is a silent no-op whenever the window is not much bigger than the frame's canvas floor. The scale divides the window to get the canvas (App_SyncUiScale, src/app.c:30430-30444) and App_SetCanvasSize then clamps back up to App_CanvasFloorWidth / APP_CANVAS_MIN_H (src/app.c:30046-30059). On the 765x503 window every 2004-era user actually runs, 150% asks for a 510x335 canvas, gets clamped to 765x503, and NOTHING on screen changes -- while the dropdown keeps reading '150%' and preferences.ini keeps 27=150. The plugin offers 13 rows (100..400 by 25, client_settings.c:35-43) and gives the user no way to know which of them can take effect; no API reports the achievable scale. On the 2004 lane this is the plugin's whole reason to exist (torirs_plugin_types.h:915-917), and no prior receipt exercised the ui_scale row at all -- they all only picked ui_scale_filter.

L4-cs-pick-scale/m01/log.txt  PLUGIN_PANEL_WIDGET index=2 kind=3 id=ui_scale label=Interface scaling selected=2 value=150 text=150   (the row says 150%)
L4-cs-pick-scale/m01/out.bmp is 807x503 -- the same canvas geometry as the 100% control L4-cs-frames/m01/out.bmp (807x503). Nothing was scaled.

items.behaviour: The status label under the Gameframe dropdown tells the user what the host actually committed
items.defect: With a saved preferred_frame of 'core/native' AND real frame providers registered (the shipped roster), plugin_frame_resolve reports status=3 FALLBACK and cs_frame_detail's FALLBACK branch (client_settings.c:170-172) prints a sentence that contradicts itself: 'Could not use Native gameframe. Active fallback: Native gameframe. The requested gameframe is not installed in this build.' The client IS running the native gameframe. The plugin also appends core/native to the dropdown as an enabled, pickable row titled 'Native gameframe' (client_settings.c:122-131) whose comment claims 'rs289lc saves it' -- but nothing in the client ever writes core/native to preferences.ini (RS_Prefs_SetPreferredFrame is reached only from api_frame_select and the migration, whose outputs are 'auto' or a catalogue id); it is a synthetic resolver sentinel that reached the file because tools/gameframe_matrix.sh:158,225 printf-writes it. The special case was derived from a harness artefact and is wrong in the very case it was written for. Prior receipts hid this because they ran TORIRS_PLUGIN_ONLY=client-settings, leaving the catalogue empty so the resolver returns early at host.c:5036 and the status stays NATIVE.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION probe: panel.set_options refuses a changed option count (host.c:5319), so a pick that adds or drops the saved-id row must fall back to panel.invalidate and rebuild the whole page
items.defect: The mechanism is real -- the pick below moves the dropdown from 6 rows (auto + 4 offers + the appended core/native row) to 5, which host.c:5319 rejects, so client_settings.c:209 clears and rebuilds the page. But the rebuild is invisible to this harness: the page comes back with the right rows and the right selection, and the two things a rebuild actually costs a user (scroll position and an open dropdown) have no headless observable, nor does the exit dump record whether set_options returned INVALID. items.behaviour: When a feature-flag config is changed from outside the page (any PluginHost_ConfigSet -- the settings face, an external editor, another plugin), the open page must show the new state
items.defect: ff_on_config_changed (src/plugin/plugins/feature_flags.c:277-287) re-applies all 16 flags to the engine but never calls ff_publish_option or panel.invalidate, so the retained rows are never re-read. After a config write of camera_arrow_keys=Off the engine reports readback=0 and plugin_prefs.ini records 'camera_arrow_keys=Off', while the open page still says 'Revision default (On)'. The page's whole purpose is to answer 'what is the client doing', and in this state it answers wrongly and silently: no error, no log (core.log is gated behind TORIRS_PLUGIN_LOG, host.c:922), no visual cue. Only closing and reopening the page fixes it. Note this is the same callback the host fires for the plugin's OWN config.set (host.c:1638-1643), which is why a pick looks fine -- the pick's own ff_publish_option at :272 papers over it.

items.behaviour: The 'Revision default (...)' entry names the value actually in force, so the page answers 'what is this client doing'
items.defect: On the 2004 lane the Draw distance row reads 'Revision default (0)'. The LostCity feature table sets painter_draw_distance = 0 (src/features/features.c:44), which is the era's way of saying 'Client-TS's fixed 25' -- ToriRS_Features_PainterDrawDistance maps 0 -> TORIRS_PAINTER_DRAW_DISTANCE_MIN = 25 (features.c:297-303). feature_flags.c:141-142 takes the INT branch and prints the raw number, so the one row that exists to report the draw distance reports a number that is not a draw distance, is outside the row's own 25..90 option list, and is 25 tiles wrong. It is revision-asymmetric: osrs239 reads 'Revision default (32 tiles)' because 32 is a named option there. No previous receipt could catch it because the exit dump prints only id/label/selected/value (main.c:3554) and never option LABELS.

items.defect: At the plugin's own declared width (TORIRS_PANEL_WIDTH_DEFAULT = 320, feature_flags.c:204-208) the internal-canvas executor clips most 'Revision default (...)' captions mid-word, so the user cannot read the value in force for the majority of rows. src/plugin/test/feature_flags_test.c pins 'captioned short enough to fit' against a fake with no text metrics, so the gate passes while the shipped page truncates. Same class in client-settings: the 'note' label always renders as 'Scaling draws the whole canvas larger, the 3D scene' with 'included.' cut off, and the FALLBACK status sentence is cut before its reason clause. Caveat I could not settle headlessly: this is the in-canvas buffer executor. The webview/aux-window executors may wrap or size differently, so the severity depends on which executor a given user runs.

items.behaviour: The cost of wearing the frame. Turning ANY gameframe-layout offer on costs 7.7x the frame time on the rev-239 lane: 4.11 ms native -> 31.84 ms Classic Fixed / 31.32 ms Modern Resizable, dropping the client from 50 fps to 30 fps.
items.defect: With a gameframe-layout frame active the client's per-frame cost goes from 4.11 ms to ~31.5 ms and effective FPS from 243.3 to ~31.5, so the pacer can no longer hold its 50 fps target and measured FPS falls to 30.0. A player who picks Classic Fixed or Modern Resizable on the OldSchool lane loses 40% of their frame rate for a cosmetic frame. It is NOT the per-frame chat dressing the code map suspects (src/plugin/plugins/gameframe.c:3375-3457, called unconditionally from frame_on_frame_start:3794): Modern Resizable never enters the dressed path and costs the same 31.32 ms. It is not a widget-count explosion either -- the exit census is 124 EMIT_EXIT / 6940 BOUNDS native against 132 / 7000 with the frame. And it is lane-specific: the same plugin frame on rs289lc costs 5.95 ms. So the cost is in what providing the frame does to the rev-239 lane's redraw (UITree_FrameProvide releasing the clipping containers, and the owned-image chain anchored OVER the scene), not in the number of things drawn.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION: frame_place_chat is the one placement helper that does not add ctx->origin_x/origin_y, so a non-zero origin would leave the chatbox at the raw canvas coordinate while every other surface, blit and stone moved.
items.defect: The defect is real in the source -- gameframe.c:954-967 uses frame_surface_at, which does not add the origin, while frame_surface (:920-927) and frame_surface_member (:929-940) both do -- but no shipped configuration can produce a non-zero origin, so no run settles it. The two producers are (a) event->safe, which app_plugin_platform_safe_rect (torirs_plugin_bridge.u.c:4510-4525) hard-codes to '*out_x = 0; *out_y = 0;' on every platform including mobile, and (b) a LEFT-docked lane_chrome_0 in frame_usable_canvas (:3624-3628), where the only lane_chrome_0 in the tree is '[role:lane_chrome_0] match=iface(popout, 1)' (revconfig/osrs239/osrs239_dat2_cache.ini:1106-1107), the 42-column rail the cache docks on the RIGHT. The right-dock branch adjusts *width only and leaves origin_x at 0.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION: frame_chat_dress runs a full role sweep -- up to 10 finds plus bounds on the bar and eight plates, each running UITree_EnsureLayoutFor -- every rendered frame while the OldSchool chat is dressed, contradicting the file's own cost claim at gameframe.c:100-104.
items.defect: The sweep is real in the source and is called unconditionally from frame_on_frame_start:3794, but I could not attribute any measurable part of the frame cost to it and the harness has no per-callback timing. The A/B that would have settled it points the other way: Modern Resizable on osrs239 never enters the dressed path and costs 31.32 ms against Classic Fixed's 31.84 ms -- 0.52 ms, under 2% of the 27.7 ms regression. So either the dressing is cheap relative to the frame's real cost or both share a larger one, and the harness cannot separate them (no plugin-callback profile, and TORIRS_PERF is not a usable measurement on this tree).

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map: native_captions is a one-way latch). Switching the client's own ground-items row off (varbit 14869) AFTER the plugin has latched onto the native caption lane must not leave the user with no labels at all.
items.defect: script/plugins/ground_items.lua:531-538 sets native_captions = true on the first groundItemCaption callback, removes its @tree watch and un-hides every native caption; :659 then gates its own drawing on `not native_captions`, and only on_stop (:505-509) ever clears the flag. The latch records 'a native lane exists', but nothing tells it the lane went away. When varbit 14869 goes to 0, app_ground_items_tick still runs script 7226 per dirty tile (src/app.c:5270-5320) and the script DESTROYS the overlay instead of building it, so no callback arrives and the plugin never re-arms its Lua lane. The user sees: enable the plugin, turn the native 'Ground items' row off in All Settings, and every label disappears -- the client's captions are gone because the setting says so, and the plugin's are gone because it thinks the client is doing the job. There is no diagnostic and the only recovery is disabling and re-enabling the plugin.

original_record.behaviour: SUSPICION (map: native_captions is a one-way latch). Switching the client's own ground-items row off (varbit 14869) AFTER the plugin has latched onto the native caption lane must not leave the user with no labels at all.
original_record.defect: script/plugins/ground_items.lua:531-538 sets native_captions = true on the first groundItemCaption callback, removes its @tree watch and un-hides every native caption; :659 then gates its own drawing on `not native_captions`, and only on_stop (:505-509) ever clears the flag. The latch records 'a native lane exists', but nothing tells it the lane went away. When varbit 14869 goes to 0, app_ground_items_tick still runs script 7226 per dirty tile (src/app.c:5270-5320) and the script DESTROYS the overlay instead of building it, so no callback arrives and the plugin never re-arms its Lua lane. The user sees: enable the plugin, turn the native 'Ground items' row off in All Settings, and every label disappears -- the client's captions are gone because the setting says so, and the plugin's are gone because it thinks the client is doing the job. There is no diagnostic and the only recovery is disabling and re-enabling the plugin.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map): a filtered/out-of-range pile writes an EMPTY caption instead of hiding the row, so the native buttons and despawn timer stay on screen measuring a zero-width caption.
items.defect: The first half is confirmed -- ground_items.lua:570 writes "" and the row stays alive: 'NATIVE_GROUND_CAPTION root=6933 node=6934 painted=0 box=85,156,350,17 color=808080 len=0'. The second half I could not reach: every capture I made reported 'buttons=0 live_buttons=0' on the NATIVE_GROUND_OVERLAY line, i.e. the cache's edit controls and despawn timers were off (varbits 14871/14873 at their defaults), so there was nothing to land on top of an empty caption. items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map): the `shape` enum is published with choices but never validated on write, and a bad value faults on_draw_world and disables the whole plugin.
items.defect: The host accepted a value that is not in the schema it published. PluginHost_ConfigSet (src/plugin/torirs_plugin_host.c:1617) and PluginHost_ConfigApply (:7285) never check `choices`, so `shape=box` -- a hand edit of plugin_prefs.ini, which host.c:1549's own comment invites -- is stored and reported applied. The first on_draw_world then raises at entity_highlighter.lua:92 through lua_world_hull (torirs_plugin_lua.c:1557 luaL_error "unknown hull shape '%s'"), which lua_script_fault turns into a permanent self-disable. The user's whole highlighter turns itself off, mid-session, on a one-word typo, with the only trace being a line in the client log. The plugin does not normalise the value and the host does not enforce the schema it advertises; either side would have fixed it.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map): TORIRS_PLUGIN_CONFIG_VALUE_MAX (192) truncates the joined tags csv on write, silently losing a tag.
items.defect: Confirmed, and it is silent data loss of the user's own saved state. save_tags (entity_highlighter.lua:66-73) rebuilds the whole csv and hands it to api.config.set; lua_config_set snprintfs it into char value[192] (torirs_plugin_lua.c:705-711), which TRUNCATES; plugin_config_value_valid (host.c:644-648) only tests strlen < 192, so the truncated string passes and is stored, and the write is reported as applied. I preloaded 32 tags (191 chars) and then tagged one more npc through the menu: the persisted list came back one id short. The user tagged Romeo and lost npc 10032 with no warning anywhere -- no log line, no rejected write, no visible change until the hull they were relying on stops appearing. Because the concat is numerically sorted, adding a LOW id pushes the HIGHEST tag off the end, so the loss is not even at the point of the edit. With a different mix of id widths the cut lands inside an id instead (e.g. '...,10477' -> '...,104'), which load_tags then parses as a real species -- the same write both loses a tag and invents one.
evidence: input: tags=10001,10002,...,10032  (32 ids, exactly 191 characters)
sim_plugin_config: frame=450 id=entity-highlighter key=tags applied=1
sim_menu_row: frame=580 row 'Tag @yel@Romeo' move 177,141
items.command: TAGS=$(python3 -c "print(','.join(str(i) for i in range(10001,10033)))"); cd /private/tmp/3draster-critic && env REPO=/private/tmp/3draster-critic BIN=/private/tmp/3draster-critic/src/torirs_critic MANIFEST=/private/tmp/plugin-engine-prepared-actions.ini TORIRSSERVER_CONTENT=/private/tmp/plugin-engine-content/osrs239-content GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=lua:entity-highlighter GF_MATRIX_TAGS=m01 GF_MATRIX_MAX_FRAMES=740 TORIRS_MINIMENU_DEBUG=1 TORIRS_SIM_PLUGIN_CONFIG="450,entity-highlighter,tags,$TAGS" TORIRS_SIM_KEYHOLD=42 TORIRS_SIM_KEYHOLD_FRAME=540 TORIRS_SIM_CLICK_NPC="560,5037,1" TORIRS_SIM_MENU_ROW="580,Tag" GF_MATRIX_EXPECT_LOG="sim_menu_row: released" zsh tools/gameframe_matrix.sh /private/tmp/critic-runs/gieh-eh-truncate
items.negative_control: /private/tmp/critic-runs/eh-osrs-menu/m01 -- the identical menu-pick attack with an EMPTY starting tag list: the persisted line is 'tags=5037', complete and intact. The only differing input is the length of the preloaded list.
items.refutation_correction: The claim is right and, if anything, understates it in one respect: the truncation does not always drop a whole id. When the cut falls inside a number it leaves a partial id that reparses as a DIFFERENT npc (run C2 persisted a bogus tag "10"), so the user can lose a tag and gain a highlight on a species they never tagged. The practical ceiling is ~31 five-digit ids.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map): the plugin only ever sees the first 16 minimenu rows (TORIRS_PLUGIN_MENU_ROWS_MAX), so on a crowded pick the npc you right-clicked can get no Tag row.
items.defect: I could not build a pick with more than 16 native rows from either fixture, so the suspicion stands unproven -- but the margin is thin and I measured it. The busiest pick I got was the rs289 throne room: two players (four rows each), two Men, two locs = 14 native rows, with the plugin's 'Tag @yel@Man' landing at row[13]. Two more rows of anything and the second Man's rows would fall past index 15 and its Tag row would silently not exist, indistinguishable from the shift gate not firing. To settle it the harness needs a scene with three-plus multi-op npcs plus a loc plus a ground pile under one cursor, and a --menu-row rule asserting a Tag row for the LAST npc in the build.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map): on the mobile gameframe there is no shift key, so the Tag/Untag rows are unreachable while plugin_prefs.mobile.ini ships the plugin enabled with tags preloaded -- hulls you cannot add to or remove.
items.defect: The harness cannot reproduce the defect, and that is the finding. TORIRS_SIM_KEYHOLD=42 injects a shift key-down straight into the command bus regardless of the client type, so api.input.key_held("shift") returns true on root 601 and the Untag row appeared normally. On a real phone there is no key to hold, so the row never appears; there is no capability check in entity_highlighter.lua:106 and no alternative gesture. What I CAN confirm from the run is the other half: with tags preloaded the plugin does draw hulls on the mobile toplevel (mesh_hull PASS pixels=116 at root 601), so a phone user genuinely ends up with outlines and, absent a keyboard, no way to remove them from the world. Settling it properly needs a headless knob that reports the platform's real modifier availability, or a touch-lane gesture in the plugin.

items.behaviour: After a toplevel remount the 'rearm' setting stops reaching the tree: the config still reads true (and is on disk) but the control's menu row is back to the original wording.
items.defect: src/plugin/plugins/widget_demo.c:124-134: on_config_changed is the ONLY place that installs the re-armed label, and it fires only on the config edit. The viewport BOUND branch at :98-103 recreates the control after every rebind and unconditionally arms it with the ORIGINAL label, never re-reading 'rearm'. So any toplevel remount (client_layout_mode change, a resize that reflows the frame, a provided-gameframe switch) silently reverts a setting that still reads true in the panel and on disk. The handler also early-returns at :129 with no log at all when state->control is not yet created, so toggling the key before the viewport binds is indistinguishable from a broken host. This is the reference plugin for the widget contract, so it is teaching the wrong shape.

live.original_criteria: src/plugin/plugins/widget_demo.c:124-134: on_config_changed is the ONLY place that installs the re-armed label, and it fires only on the config edit. The viewport BOUND branch at :98-103 recreates the control after every rebind and unconditionally arms it with the ORIGINAL label, never re-reading 'rearm'. So any toplevel remount (client_layout_mode change, a resize that reflows the frame, a provided-gameframe switch) silently reverts a setting that still reads true in the panel and on disk. The handler also early-returns at :129 with no log at all when state->control is not yet created, so toggling the key before the viewport binds is indistinguishable from a broken host. This is the reference plugin for the widget contract, so it is teaching the wrong shape.

items.behaviour: The obvious way to run just the demo, TORIRS_PLUGIN_ONLY=widget-demo (what GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=widget-demo exports), starts a client with ZERO plugins and says nothing.
items.defect: src/plugin/torirs_plugin_registry.c:90-97. TORIRS_PLUGIN_ONLY=<anything not in PLUGIN_TABLE> registers nothing and returns silently -- no log line, no host error, exit 0. The comment ('The capture gate rejects a missing selected plugin') offloads the failure onto a harness rule that only exists when someone remembers to pass --plugin-id, and a person running the client by hand gets no signal at all. The same door is the only way to select a plugin, so a typo in any plugin id has the same effect. Per CLAUDE.md this is precisely the silent-return shape: the caller's bad input should abort loudly here, not produce a plausible-looking client with no plugins.
evidence: exit-status 0 -- the client booted, logged in, ran 620 frames and exited cleanly
grep -c PLUGIN_STATE log.txt -> 0. Not one plugin was registered; the exit dump loop at src/main.c:3369 has nothing to iterate.
grep -c 'PLUGIN' log.txt -> 2, and neither is an error: there is no diagnostic anywhere naming the plugin that could not be found

items.behaviour: TORIRS_WIDGET_DEMO is a presence test, not a value test: setting it to 0 turns the demo ON (and additionally registers the whole shipped table).
items.defect: src/plugin/torirs_plugin_registry.c:99-108. One overloaded env var carries three different behaviours ('lua' -> Lua host instead; 'only' -> demo alone; anything else including '0'/'false'/'off' -> demo PLUS the whole table), selected by presence for the third. Setting it to 0 to turn the probe off enables it. Minor because it is a developer knob, but it is the knob every widget-contract receipt was captured through, and 'the demo was off' is not something a reader can conclude from the variable's value.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map: 'STYLES[style] is indexed with an unvalidated config string'). Setting style to a value outside the declared choices must not be able to kill the plugin.
items.defect: PluginHost_ConfigSet (src/plugin/torirs_plugin_host.c:1616-1645) validates only that the key matches [a-z0-9_] and that the value is one INI line; it never checks the value against ToriRS_ConfigItem.choices, and never clamps an int against min/max. script/plugins/loot_beam.lua:208 (model_for) then does STYLES[style].asset on a nil table, the Lua call faults, lua_script_flush_disable switches the plugin off and the host tears down its scene objects. Both entry points reach it: an api.config.set / scheduled settings edit (main.c's TORIRS_SIM_PLUGIN_CONFIG comment even calls it 'the normal validated config API'), and a hand-edited plugin_prefs.ini, which is a plain text file the host itself writes and users are expected to read. The plugin never comes back for that session and the user is told nothing.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map: 'Hidden metrics are still positioned, landing exactly on top of the next visible line'). Turning a metric off should leave nothing behind.
items.defect: script/plugins/performance_display.lua:126-134 calls set_position/set_size on every metric BEFORE the 'if api.config[metric.visible] then row = row + 1' guard, so a disabled metric keeps a real 132x15 owned node at the coordinates of the next visible row. Two owned text nodes therefore share one rectangle. Nothing hides the node (hidden=0) and nothing removes it. The moment an owned text node grows a background, a border, an op or a hit box -- which is a normal thing for the widget API to gain -- these become stacked click targets over the scene, and the register's reading of this same capture ('exactly two magenta lines') is true of ink, not of nodes.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map: 'UIELEM_BUILTIN_WORLD does not clip its children, so a large x/y paints the readout over the surround/inventory'). What actually happens at an in-range x that exceeds the viewport width.
items.defect: The schema declares x/y with min 0 max 4096 (script/plugins/performance_display.lua:49-50) on a surface that is 512 px wide on the fixed 548 and 2004 frames. Any value in the top three quarters of the declared range silently blanks the entire readout, and PluginHost_ConfigSet clamps nothing (torirs_plugin_host.c:1616-1645 checks only key charset and value shape). Worse for a debugger: the engine's own exit dump still reports all four nodes hidden=0 with non-zero text length at box=604,32, so anyone diagnosing 'my readout disappeared' from the trace is told it is visible. Either the schema max should be the viewport extent, or the plugin should clamp against the bound widget's size (which it already resolves) -- it does neither.

items.behaviour: SUSPICION (map, loot_tracker.c:2199,2243,1963,2075-2103): 'two widths' - on_ui_layout stores the whole panel's logical width in g_well_w while the paint and the right-anchored hit boxes use the custom REGION width, so a totals-band click after a layout event lands on the wrong button.
items.defect: Not reproducible headlessly, and I am saying so rather than clearing it. The mismatch is real in the source, but g_well_w is overwritten with the region width on EVERY draw pass, so the window in which the layout width is live is one frame wide (or the pre-first-draw value 320). The harness has no way to inject a click inside that single frame - TORIRS_SIM_CLICK_AT lands on a frame boundary and the draw has already run. What is missing to reach it: a knob that fires a panel layout event and a click in the same frame, or an on_ui_layout that reported the custom width.

items.behaviour: The special-attack orb on a revision whose own profile says there is no special-attack interface.
items.defect: minimap_orbs.c:1058-1064 resolves the special id as config -> [varp:special_attack_energy] -> historical constant 300, with no lane check; rs289lc declares no such varp, so the fallback 300 is read and whatever a LostCity world happens to keep there is rendered as a special-attack meter. The orb draws '60' on a 2004 world that has no special attack. items.behaviour: What happens on the frame the orb roles bind (map SUSPICION: watches fire in registration order, so the plugin builds four beside-map controls and immediately destroys them).
items.defect: Confirmed. orbs_start registers the 'minimap' watch first (minimap_orbs.c:1127-1129), so on a fresh publication the minimap BOUND arrives before any orb-role BOUND and orbs_layout takes the beside-map branch with all four native_root refs still zero. Each of the four orb roles then arrives separately, and every arrival re-runs a full orbs_layout with a changed parent - remove + create + up to four whole-tree widgets.revalidate calls (:1022, which bridge:4063-4065 maps to UITree_EnsureLayout on the entire tree). My run publishes 42 MINIMAP_ORBS_CONTROL lines at boot for four orbs, 20 of them at the WRONG (beside-map) coordinates. Any frame presented mid-sequence shows orbs 3-10px out of place; the rest is pure cost, repeated on every gameframe rebuild.

items.behaviour: What the globes do to the 3D scene underneath them.
items.defect: Every globe is armed with an operation (xp_orbs.c:1776 set_on_op on EVERY globe), so it is native-input-present and it does not merely ADD a 'Flip' row over the world - it REPLACES the world rows entirely. Right-clicking the exact same scene pixel with a globe present offers 'Flip' and 'Cancel' and nothing else; with no globe it offers 'Chop down Tree' twice, 'Walk here' and 'Examine Tree' twice. Five 46x46 armed squares across the top centre of the viewport (up to 230x46 in a row) therefore make that strip of the scene completely un-interactable - no walking, no chopping, no examining - and the reference this plugin ports (RuneLite XpGlobes) has no menu entry at all. The armed box is the full square while the visual hover is the inscribed disc, so the corners steal the click without even darkening.

items.behaviour: A user who switches client layout (the Modern Resizable toplevel) while the plugin is running loses the Screenshots plugin entirely - camera, hotkey, and all eleven automatic event captures - with no message anywhere in the client.
items.defect: script/plugins/screenshot.lua:152 `assert(report:set_hidden(replace))` inside update_controls. A live root remount re-resolves the report_button role and delivers the watch event while the `report` upvalue still holds the pre-remount node ref; set_hidden answers STALE_REFERENCE, which is a legitimate runtime state, not a contract violation. The Lua assert faults, src/plugin/torirs_plugin_lua.c:1112 -> lua_script_fault -> lua_script_defer_disable, and the WHOLE plugin is disabled (PLUGIN_STATE enabled=0 running=0 error=1). It happens with the camera at its shipped default 'off' as well, because the `if report then ... set_hidden(false)` arm runs in every mode - so it hits every user who has the plugin on (the shipped default) the first time they change layout. The user sees nothing: the Report button comes back via owner teardown, the chat bar looks normal, and the plugin's real feature (auto-capturing level-ups, pets, boss kills, clue caskets, drops) is dead for the rest of the session.

Every value from 53 to 512 that the settings row happily accepts is unreachable, silently. A user who types a familiar number (112 for an ASCII 'p', an SDL scancode, an OSRS key id) gets a setting that does nothing and no feedback of any kind. The enum also has no F-keys or PrintScreen, so the conventional screenshot keys cannot be bound at all.

items.behaviour: Captures are filed under the player's name.
items.defect: Every capture on the 2004 lane lands in a folder literally called 'invalid-name'. Two things meet: src/net/jbase37.c:6 guards base37 names against MAX_BASE37 = 0x1000000000000000 (2^60) with the comment '12 characters in base37', but 37^12 = 6.58e18 > 2^60, so any 12-character name above 2^60 decodes to the sentinel string 'invalid_name'; and script/plugins/screenshot.lua:68-72 treats 'name is non-empty' as 'name is real' and slugs the sentinel straight into the path. This is not a harness artefact - it is what a user with a 12-character login sees. It also silently merges every such player's captures into one shared folder.

items.behaviour: The mouse-over outline traces the object you are pointing at.
items.defect: It does not trace it - it draws a coarse convex hull that swallows whatever is standing nearby, the player included. src/plugin/plugins/nxt_highlight.c:119 hardcodes TORIRS_HULL_MESH, whose implementation is a 16-direction extreme-point convex hull (APP_OUTLINE_HULL_MESH_DIRECTIONS 16, src/app.c:3594, :3624). For any concave or slender subject the hull encloses instead of tracing, and because the outline sits in the screen-space entity-overlay layer with no depth test, anything drawn in front of the subject lands inside the outline. The API's own guidance (src/plugin/torirs_plugin_api.h:875-884) says BOUNDS 'stays the default and the sane choice for marking a crowd'; the plugin has no config (state_size 0, config NULL) so a user cannot change it. Separately, the group's outline_width=2 is read as a boolean at nxt_highlight.c:63-67 and the draw verbs take no thickness parameter at all, so a thickness-1 and a thickness-2 group are indistinguishable on screen.

items.defect: It is not. In /private/tmp/critic-runs/bn1-osrs-toggle/m01 two bird_nest_egg_red were dropped on the same tile (520 and 600) with the plugin enabled from frame 560; the second drop produced no notice at all, while in bn4 the identical timing with a DIFFERENT nest id (bird_nest_seeds) at 600 did notify. The plugin's only input is on_item_spawn (APP_PLUGIN_ITEM_SPAWN from PKT_NAME_OBJ_ADD/OBJ_REVEAL, src/app.c:34055-34081), so a same-id drop that merges into the existing ground stack raises no spawn and the plugin never hears about it. In play: two red-egg nests under you and only the first is announced. It is the mirror of the other half of this class the map flagged - the plugin holds no state (state_size 0, `(void)state` at nxt_bird_nest.c:90) so it can neither de-duplicate a re-sent OBJ_ADD on a region rebuild nor notice a second genuine one.

rows.behaviour: The status label under the Gameframe dropdown tells the user what the host actually committed

result.claim: With a saved preferred_frame of "core/native" and real frame providers registered, plugin_frame_resolve reports status=3 FALLBACK and cs_frame_detail prints the self-contradicting "Could not use Native gameframe. Active fallback: Native gameframe. The requested gameframe is not installed in this build." while the client is in fact running the native gameframe; the plugin also appends core/native as a sixth enabled, pickable dropdown row on the strength of a comment ("rs289lc saves it") that is false, since nothing in the client ever writes core/native to preferences.ini.
result.what_i_ran:
Five runs of my own, all with the client-settings page opened by TORIRS_SIM_PLUGIN_PANEL="120,client-settings,page" and TORIRS_PLUGIN_LOG=1.
(1) Counter-case, harness, OSRS239 m05, full roster, harness-written preferred_frame=gameframe-layout/modern-fixed -> ref-osrs-m05-roster.
(2) Counter-case, harness, rs289lc r01 with GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=client-settings (the harness's OWN default preferred_frame there is core/native) -> ref-rs289-native.
(3) Counter-case, harness, rs289lc r01 with GF_MATRIX_RS289_FRAME=gameframe-layout/classic-fixed (full roster, providers registered) -> ref-rs289-classic. This one exists to prove providers DO register on rs289lc, since the harness refuses to combine core/native with the roster (tools/gameframe_matrix.sh sets BASELINE=1 whenever rs_frame==core/native, and TORIRS_PLUGIN_ONLY takes exactly one id, so no harness capture can produce the claimed state).
(4) Repro, OSRS239: because FRAMES_LIST holds no core/native, I rebuilt the harness's exact invocation by hand in a fresh dir (same TORIRS_PREFS/TORIRSSERVER_SAVES/TORIRS_PLUGIN_PREFS/SDL dummy/620 frames/EXIT_BMP, full roster, MANIFEST=/private/tmp/plugin-engine-prepared-actions.ini) with preferences.ini preferred_frame=core/native -> ref-native-pref/m05n.
(5) Repro, rs289lc: same manual reconstruction including the harness's per-run LostCity account allocation and rs289-seed.sav, preferred_frame=core/native, full roster -> ref-rs289-nativepref/r01n.
I also read the frames as 2x/cropped PNGs, and traced the writers of the preference in source (src/game/rs_prefs.c, src/plugin/torirs_plugin_bridge.u.c:2582 app_plugin_frame_preference_set, src/plugin/torirs_plugin_host.c:1203 api_frame_select, src/plugin/plugins/client_settings.c:295-330 cs_frame_known gate).
result.what_i_saw:
Repro OSRS239 (ref-native-pref/m05n/log.txt):
  frame_selection: requested=core/native active=core/native status=3 reason=The requested gameframe is not installed in this build.
  PLUGIN_PANEL_WIDGET index=0 kind=3 id=gameframe label=Gameframe selected=5 value=core/native text=core/native
  PLUGIN_PANEL_WIDGET index=1 kind=0 id=gameframe_detail text=Could not use Native gameframe. Active fallback: Native gameframe. The requested gameframe is not installed in this build.
selected=5 is the sixth row (auto + four providers + the appended core/native sentinel), and it is enabled.
Repro rs289lc (ref-rs289-nativepref/r01n/log.txt): identical - status=3, same sentence, selected=5. So "revision: both" holds.
Pixels: in both out.bmp captures the Client Settings window shows the Gameframe dropdown reading "Native gameframe" with, directly under it, "Could not use Native gameframe. Active fallback: Na" (the label clips at the pane width), while the surrounding screen is unmistakably the lane's own native gameframe, fully up and rendering. So the contradiction is on screen, not only in the log.
Counter-cases all read correctly, so the sentence is specific to this state, not a constant: m05 full roster -> "Active: Modern Fixed." (status=1); rs289lc classic-fixed full roster -> "Active: Classic Fixed." (status=1); rs289lc core/native with the plugin isolated (empty frame catalogue, so plugin_frame_resolve returns early at torirs_plugin_host.c:5052) -> "Active: Native gameframe.", selected=1.
Contamination check: none of the repro evidence depends on the scorer; the two harness OSRS/rs289 captures scored 0 failures with no world_session_live=FAIL line, and the panel text is emitted by the plugin itself.
Provenance of the state, which I verified in source rather than assuming: the only writer of preferred_frame is api_frame_select -> app_plugin_frame_preference_set, reached from client_settings' pick handler, which is gated by cs_frame_known - and the core/native row exists only when core/native is ALREADY the requested id. So the client never writes it itself; the value arrives from a hand-edited preferences.ini (the file's own header advertises hand-editing), from a third-party Lua plugin calling frame.select (lua_frame_select passes it, since plugin_frame_preference_id_valid accepts "core/native"), or from tools/gameframe_matrix.sh, which writes preferred_frame=core/native for every rs289lc r01 run - and that harness default, not the client, is what the code comment at client_settings.c:123 mistakes for "rs289lc saves it". The claim already states both preconditions, so this narrows nothing it asserted.

rows.behaviour: When a feature-flag config is changed from outside the page (any PluginHost_ConfigSet -- the settings face, an external editor, another plugin), the open page must show the new state
rows.correction: The stale row is real and I saw it, but the trigger list in the claim is wrong: in this build there is no shipped user gesture that can produce it for feature-flags. The ONLY dispatch site for on_config_changed is PluginHost_ConfigSet (torirs_plugin_host.c:1641), and its only callers in the client are (a) the plugin's own api->config.set, which is scoped to the calling plugin's own index (api_cfg_set, host.c:1656) — for feature-flags that is ff_on_ui_action, which does call ff_publish_option, so the pick path is correct (run B proves it), and (b) app_plugin_panel_save (torirs_plugin_panel.u.c:1631-1665), which writes only DECLARED ToriRS_ConfigItem rows and then calls PluginHost_Reload; feature-flags declares no config items at all, so its settings face writes nothing. "An external editor" is also not a route: prefs are decoded once by PluginHost_ConfigDecode in Task_PluginBoot BEFORE PluginHost_Start (task_plugin_io.c:273-286), when no plugin is running and no page exists, so no on_config_changed fires and the later-built page reads the store correctly (run D). The only writer that reaches a running plugin with its page open is the headless drive hook TORIRS_SIM_PLUGIN_CONFIG (main.c:1719). So: a real latent hole in the plugin-engine contract (a host that notifies on_config_changed but never invalidates the retained page, and a plugin that does not invalidate for itself), user-visible only under the test harness. Severity minor, not major.

result.what_i_ran:
Four of my own captures, each in a fresh dir, plus a source read.

1) /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-ff-dd-1 — rs289lc, GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=feature-flags, TORIRS_SIM_PLUGIN_PANEL="60,feature-flags,page", TORIRS_TRACE_NATIVE_UI=1. Panel opens at the top of the list.
2) /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-ff-dd-2 — same plus TORIRS_SIM_WHEEL="480,160,250,-1,10". (The wheel landed on a dropdown and flipped Camera distance to "Further (130)" instead of scrolling — discarded, but it proves the collapsed box paints the OPTION LABEL, not the stored value.)
3) /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-ff-dd-3 (PRIMARY) — rs289lc, same panel drive plus TORIRS_SIM_DRAG="470,307,150,307,300" to pull the panel scrollbar thumb down so the Scene section is on screen. Cropped (0,60)-(340,340) at 3x and read the image.
4) /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-ff-dd-osrs and .../ref-ff-dd-osrs2 — the counter-case: osrs239, GF_MATRIX_TAGS=m03, identical panel drive and identical scrollbar drag.
5) /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-ff-dd-pick25 — rs289lc with TORIRS_SIM_PANEL_PICK="120,feature-flags,draw_distance,25", the "same value, named explicitly" counter-case.

Source read to check the number the label omits: src/features/features.h:116 (TORIRS_PAINTER_DRAW_DISTANCE_MIN = 25), src/features/features.c:297-306, src/app.c:18951 (painter_set_draw_distance of that resolved value), src/plugin/torirs_plugin_bridge.u.c:2127-2142 (the registry row: min 25, max 90, choices "25 tiles|...|90 tiles"), src/plugin/plugins/feature_flags.c:131-138 (named-choice branch vs raw-%d INT branch).
result.what_i_saw:
It is user-visible and I saw it in the frame, not just in the source.

rs289lc (ref-ff-dd-3/r01/out.bmp, after the scrollbar drag): under the "Scene" heading the row paints

    Draw distance    [ Revision default (0) ]

osrs239 m03 (ref-ff-dd-osrs2/m03/out.bmp), same drive, same drag, same row position:

    Draw distance    [ Revision default (32 tiles) ]

So the revision asymmetry is exactly as claimed, and it is not a rendering accident: the two neighbouring rows in both captures (Movement, NPC type lighting, Chathead light) carry proper named parentheticals on both lanes.

Log corroboration from my own runs:
  ref-ff-dd-1/r01/log.txt:18   PLUGIN_FEATURE_SET key=draw_distance value=0 readback=0 default=0
  ref-ff-dd-osrs/m03/log.txt:18 PLUGIN_FEATURE_SET key=draw_distance value=32 readback=32 default=32

The number that should be there is 25: features.c:299-303 returns TORIRS_PAINTER_DRAW_DISTANCE_MIN (25) for a table value of 0, and app.c:18951 hands that resolved value straight to painter_set_draw_distance. So on the 2004 lane the row reports 0 while the painter is culling at 25 tiles.

The mechanism is confirmed too: ff_options() (feature_flags.c:133) takes the named-choice branch only when ff_value_index(flag, effective) >= 0. The registry lists {25,32,40,50,60,70,80,90}, so 0 indexes to -1 and the code falls through to the raw "%s (%d)" INT branch. 0 is also below the row's declared min of 25, so it is a value the user can never pick back by number — only "Revision default" restores it.

Counter-cases I ran, and none of them explains the reading away:
- ref-ff-dd-pick25: picking the explicitly named "25 tiles" makes the same row paint "25 tiles" and logs value=25 readback=25 default=0. Same effective distance, honest label — the row can display the truth, only the default path does not.
- osrs239 (same plugin, same tag drive, same drag) shows the correct named parenthetical, so this is not a chrome/label-truncation bug and not the harness's own default.
- Not contamination: GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=feature-flags isolates the plugin, no world_session_live=FAIL appears in either run's pixels.txt, and the only pixel failures in the osrs239 runs are the unrelated pre-existing no_captionless_2004_hollows / chat_inside_complete_surround on root 548.

Scope is display-only, which is why minor stands: picking, readback, restore-to-default and the client's actual 25-tile draw distance are all correct. One row, one lane, reports the era sentinel instead of the distance it resolves to.

The clipping is real and I saw it in the frame, on both revisions.

feature-flags, OSRS239 m01, default 320 panel. The log shows 16 dropdown rows (kind=3) and the model holds the full text. In the painted frame, 10 of those 16 captions are cut, most of them mid-word:
  Zoom               "Revision default (Mouse whe"      (Mouse wheel)
  Wheel step         "Revision default (Normal (6("     (Normal (60))
  Camera distance    "Revision default (Reference"      (Reference (100))
  Click off the map  "Revision default (Does noth"      (Does nothing)

  Chathead light     "Revision default (Scene regi"     (Scene register)

The 6 that survive are the three short ones (Zoom range, Arrow keys orbit, Draw distance) and the three that happen to use the wrapped label-above-value row (Overhead distance, Middle-button drag, Held-item spell bit), which gets the full panel width. So "the majority of rows" is exactly right: 10/16.

Counter-case, same run family, only the width changed: clicking the panel's own Fullscreen button makes every one of those captions render in full ("Revision default (Mouse wheel)", "(Reference (100))", "(70 tiles (deob))", ...). Nothing else moved, so the loss is purely the 320px column, as claimed.

rs289lc r01: identical — "Mouse whe", "Normal (6(", "Reference" cut in the same three rows. Not revision-specific.

client-settings, OSRS239 m01, isolated: reproduced verbatim. The log carries text="Scaling draws the whole canvas larger, the 3D scene included." and the frame paints "Scaling draws the whole canvas larger, the 3D scene" — "included." gone. It does not wrap, and there is roughly 250px of empty panel below it, so the room exists.

No contamination: pixels.txt in all five capture dirs has no FAIL line and no world_session_live failure; selected_plugin_running=PASS names the isolated plugin.

Two nuances that do not change the verdict, only the wording:
- The test citation is loose. feature_flags_test.c:1312 attaches the message "captioned short enough to fit" to strcmp(w->label, "Draw distance") — the ROW LABEL, which does fit. No test measures the option caption at all. So the gate is silent about the truncation rather than actively pinning it; the conclusion ("nothing catches it") holds, the mechanism described does not.
- The FALLBACK half I could not settle. A bogus gameframe id was ignored (the detail row still read "Active: Native gameframe. Auto follows this lane."), so I never produced the "Could not use %s. Active fallback: %s. <reason>" string on screen. By construction it is far longer than the note that already truncates, but I did not see it, and the finding's own caveat already concedes this.

result.claim: On the OSRS239 lane, turning on any gameframe-layout frame offer costs ~7.7x the per-frame work (4.11 ms native -> ~31.5 ms with Classic Fixed or Modern Resizable), dropping the client from 50 fps to 30 fps.
result.what_i_ran: Six of my own sequential captures (never parallel, new dir each), all with the optimized embedded-server binary /private/tmp/3draster-critic/src/torirs_critic (build_critic_opt_es; the OPT=0 twin torirs_critic0 was NOT used), MANIFEST=/private/tmp/plugin-engine-prepared-actions.ini, GF_MATRIX_MAX_FRAMES=900, and my own added TORIRS_FPS_REPORT=1 so I had a measure independent of the plugin overlay: (1) GF_MATRIX_TAGS=m01 (auto/native) -> ref-perf-native; (2) GF_MATRIX_TAGS=m03 (gameframe-layout/classic-fixed) -> ref-perf-classic; (3) m01 + GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=gameframe-layout (plugin loaded, frame NOT worn) -> ref-gfl-only-auto; (4) m03 + GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=gameframe-layout (frame worn, every other plugin off) -> ref-gfl-only; (5) m07 (modern-resizable) -> ref-perf-modres; (6) m09 (mobile-gameframe/stone-drawer, a DIFFERENT provider) -> ref-perf-stone. I also timed each harness invocation for process user CPU, and cropped the performance-display overlay out of each out.bmp at 4x and read it. Confounder checks: read the overlay's source (script/plugins/performance_display.lua) and its data source (api.core.frame_work_us -> App_NoteFrameTime in src/main.c:3223, which the shell closes before the pacing sleep, so it is work not wall clock); checked that the harness's TORIRS_DUMP_BOUNDS/TORIRS_DUMP_EMIT_EXIT/TORIRS_TRACE_NATIVE_UI dumps run AFTER the frame loop (src/main.c:3369-3410), and that log volume is equal between arms (15264 vs 15752 lines), so the delta is not harness logging; confirmed no FAIL rows in either pixels.txt and exit-status 0 for both.
result.what_i_saw: The effect reproduces, on my own runs, in three mutually independent measurements. Overlay, native m01: 'FPS: 50.0 / Frame: 4.04 ms / Effective FPS: 247.7'. Overlay, classic-fixed m03: 'FPS: 30.4 / Frame: 31.44 ms / Effective FPS: 31.8' (/private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-native-metrics.png, ref-classic-metrics.png). The client's own presented-frame counter agrees: [fps] settles at 48.8 native vs 30.3 with the frame. Process user CPU over the same 900 frames agrees: 8.72 s native vs 32.70 s with the frame, i.e. ~26.6 ms/frame of extra CPU, which matches the 27.4 ms overlay delta. The counter-case pins the cause on WEARING the frame, not on loading the plugin: with gameframe-layout loaded but preferred_frame=auto the run is 48.8 fps / 8.71 s CPU, identical to native; with the same single plugin and classic-fixed worn it is 30.3 fps / 32.62 s CPU, identical to the full plugin set. So no other plugin (minimap-orbs, xp-drop-orbs, performance-display) contributes. Modern Resizable m07 costs the same: 30.3 fps / 33.27 s CPU, confirming the claim's point that it is not the chat dressing path. rows.behaviour: SUSPICION (map: native_captions is a one-way latch). Switching the client's own ground-items row off (varbit 14869) AFTER the plugin has latched onto the native caption lane must not leave the user with no labels at all.

result.claim: ground_items.lua's `native_captions` is a one-way latch: once the plugin has latched onto the native CS2 caption lane, switching the client's own "Ground items" row (varbit 14869) off destroys the native overlays but never re-arms the plugin's own Lua drawing lane, so the user is left with no ground-item labels at all while the plugin still reports running.
result.what_i_ran:
Four of my own osrs239 m01 captures via tools/gameframe_matrix.sh from /private/tmp/3draster-critic, all with GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=lua:ground-items, TORIRS_PLUGIN_LOG=1 (TORIRS_TRACE_NATIVE_UI=1 is on by default in the harness):
1. /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-gi-on — plugin only, no drops (found the seeded stacks are on level 1 and off-camera, so nothing to see; discarded as a baseline).
2. /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-ctl-drop2 — CONTROL: TORIRS_SIM_CMD="500,dropobj logs 1;520,dropobj bones 1" (note: the harness prepends "::"; passing "::dropobj" gives "::::dropobj" and the server answers "debugproc not found").
3. /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-gi-varoff — REPRO: same drops + TORIRS_SIM_VARBIT="560,14869,0" (the row switched off after the latch).
4. /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-gi-varoff-recycle — COUNTER-CASE: same drops, TORIRS_SIM_VARBIT="540,14869,0", then TORIRS_SIM_PLUGIN_TOGGLE="560,ground-items,0;575,ground-items,1" so on_stop/on_start clear the latch while the row stays off.
(also /private/tmp/critic-runs/ref-gi-varoff-early with the varbit off at frame 100 — the latch already fires at world load, so it looks like case 3.)
Measured white label ink in the world crop (60,140)-(460,210) of each out.bmp and read the crops at 3x.
result.what_i_saw:
The latch is real and it is one-way, and it costs the user every label.
- Control (row on): log "[ground-items] native caption formatting active", then at exit "NATIVE_GROUND_OVERLAY root=6933 ... emitted=1 coord=52596064 captions=2 hidden_captions=0 caption_emits=1" and the frame shows "Logs (EX: 4 gp) (HA: 2 gp)" over the player's tile — 331 white pixels in the crop.
- Repro (row off at 560): same latch line, then "NATIVE_GROUND_OVERLAY root=6916 ... captions=0 caption_emits=0" and "root=6933 ... emitted=0 coord=52596064 captions=0 ... caption_emits=0" — i.e. exactly the evidence line quoted in the finding — and the frame has NO label anywhere: 15 white pixels in the crop (background speckle only). Meanwhile "PLUGIN_STATE id=ground-items enabled=1 running=1 error=0", exit-status 0, every harness PIXEL check PASS, so this is not a dead session or a crashed plugin.
- Counter-case is the decisive one: identical world, identical varbit-off state, only the plugin cycled off/on. Both native overlays still report captions=0 (the native lane is genuinely gone), yet "Logs (EX: 4 gp) (HA: 2 gp)" is painted again — 258 white pixels — by the plugin's own Lua lane. So the label the user loses is one the plugin is perfectly able to draw; the only thing withholding it is the stale `native_captions = true` gating `if sx and not native_captions` at ground_items.lua:659, which nothing but on_stop (:505-509) ever clears.
Scope, precisely: the loss lasts as long as the row stays off, and is cured either by turning the row back on or by disabling/re-enabling the plugin. Only the stacks the plugin would have labelled are affected (Bones stays invisible in both lanes because it is on the reference default hidden list).

rows.behaviour: SUSPICION (map): TORIRS_PLUGIN_CONFIG_VALUE_MAX (192) truncates the joined tags csv on write, silently losing a tag.
rows.correction: The claim is right and, if anything, understates it in one respect: the truncation does not always drop a whole id. When the cut falls inside a number it leaves a partial id that reparses as a DIFFERENT npc (run C2 persisted a bogus tag "10"), so the user can lose a tag and gain a highlight on a species they never tagged. The practical ceiling is ~31 five-digit ids.

result.claim: TORIRS_PLUGIN_CONFIG_VALUE_MAX (192) truncates entity-highlighter's joined tags csv on write, silently losing a tag: save_tags rebuilds the whole csv and api.config.set snprintfs it into char value[192] (lua_config_set), the truncated string then passes plugin_config_value_valid (strlen < 192) and is stored and reported as applied, with no warning anywhere.
result.what_i_ran:
Three OSRS239 m05 captures (tools/gameframe_matrix.sh, GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=lua:entity-highlighter, GF_MATRIX_MAX_FRAMES=900, TORIRS_PLUGIN_LOG=1), each preloading a tags csv at frame 450 and then tagging Romeo through the real menu path (TORIRS_SIM_KEYHOLD=42 shift at 460, TORIRS_SIM_CLICK_NPC="470,...,1" right-click, TORIRS_SIM_MENU_ROW="490,Tag "), reading the persisted value back from <out>/plugin_prefs.ini which the run writes itself.
A (repro): preload 10001..10032 = 32 ids, 191 chars.
B (counter-case, the same drive with a shorter list): preload 10001..10031 = 31 ids, 185 chars.
C2 (precision): preload 999,10001..10031 = 189 chars, npc pinned to type 5037 so the cut lands mid-number.
Also read the source paths myself: src/plugin/torirs_plugin_lua.c:705-711, src/plugin/torirs_plugin_host.c:644-648 and PluginHost_ConfigSet at :1617.
result.what_i_saw:
A: log shows "sim_plugin_config: frame=450 ... applied=1", "sim_menu_row: frame=490 row 'Tag @yel@Romeo'", pixels.txt mesh_hull=PASS pixels=561 and the frame shows Romeo inside a magenta mesh hull, so the tag really landed. The persisted line is tags=5037,10001,...,10031, — it ends on a trailing comma; 10032 is gone. Nothing in log.txt mentions truncation, a rejected write, or any error (grep for trunc/too long/rejected/invalid: 0 hits).
B (counter-case): identical drive, 190-char result, and the ini holds all 32 ids ending ...,10031 with 5037 added. So the loss in A is the 192 cap and not the harness, the menu path, or a moving npc.
C2: persisted line ends ...,10029,10030,10 — 10031 was lost AND a partial id "10" was left behind, which load_tags's "%d+" reads as a real tag on base npc id 10. Still no warning of any kind.
No world_session_live=FAIL in any run (the check is not emitted; the world is live and rendering, per the frame and mesh_hull=PASS).
One precision point on the mechanism: the ceiling is Lua-side. The C entry PluginHost_ConfigSet refuses a >=192-byte value (returns false); it is lua_config_set's snprintf into char value[192] that shortens the string before the validator ever sees it, so the plugin is told the write succeeded.

rows.behaviour: The plate is drawn on top of the client's own hover caption for the same cell, so two texts fight for the same pixels.
rows.correction:
The behaviour is exactly as claimed, but two parts of their explanation are wrong and should not be carried into a fix.

(a) "it is what app_hover_text_update produced from the very rows item_stats read" — no. app_hover_text_update / UIHoverText_Compose produces the TOP-LEFT viewport caption ("… / 3 more options"), which the plate never touches. The thing the plate covers is the separate rev-239 cursor tooltip (the two-line "Wear Rune platebody" / "+3 options" box), a different producer, built from the widget's menu ops, not from item_stats' stat rows.

(b) "The retired placement API … is what used to keep them apart" — false, and checkable. `git show 9f0173795^:src/plugin/plugins/item_stats.c` line 2816 is the identical `x = mouse_x + 12; y = mouse_y + 16;`. The retirement changed only the clamp rectangle used for the edge flip (placement.area(TORIRS_AREA_RAW_VIEWPORT) → the draw context's canvas bounds). The overlap is not a regression introduced by that retirement; it has been there since the plugin was written, and restoring a placement area would not fix it.

Scope: osrs239 only (the pointer-anchored cursor tooltip is a rev-239 cache feature; rs289lc has no such box), and it does not apply on a hover close enough to the right or bottom edge for the plate to flip away from the pointer.

(3) ref-is-cell2: GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=item-stats, TORIRS_SIM_MOVE_AT="400,661,228" (the neighbouring equipment cell) to test generality.
Each out.bmp cropped 3x around the equipment panel and read. I also read src/plugin/plugins/item_stats.c:2816-2838, src/ui/uitree_hovertext.c, and `git show 9f0173795^:src/plugin/plugins/item_stats.c` to test their causal story.
result.what_i_saw:
The overlap is real and I saw it in my own frames.

ref-is-base (all plugins off) settles what the client itself draws: TWO captions. One at the top-left of the viewport, "Wear Rune platebody / 3 more options" (that is UIHoverText_Compose, src/ui/uitree_hovertext.c:43). And a second, pointer-anchored two-line box "Wear Rune platebody" / "+3 options" occupying roughly source x 620..743, y 251..287 — the rev-239 cursor tooltip. It is present with zero plugins loaded, so it is not a plugin artefact or a harness default.

ref-is-plate (item-stats on, identical pointer): log.txt:1027 PLUGIN_CANVAS_IMAGE slot=1 box=629,244,82,140, i.e. x 629..711, y 244..384. That rectangle lands squarely inside the cursor tooltip's 620..743 / 251..287. In the 3x crop the plate is on top: only the leading "W" pokes out to the left of the plate and the tails "…body" and "…options" poke out to the right, with "Prayer: -1 / Range Str: -4" of the plate printed over the middle of the caption. Two texts, same pixels, plugin on top.

ref-is-cell2 reproduces it one cell over: PLUGIN_CANVAS_IMAGE box=673,244,82,140 over a caption at ~664..787 / 251..287, same shredded look. So it is not a single-cell coincidence — the caption box is anchored at about pointer+(3,+23) and the plate at pointer+(12,+16), so they must overlap on any hover that does not flip at a canvas edge.

No contamination: pixels.txt on both plugin runs shows selected_plugin_running=PASS id=item-stats and no world_session_live=FAIL line; the harness's own checks all PASS.

rows.behaviour: After a toplevel remount the 'rearm' setting stops reaching the tree: the config still reads true (and is on disk) but the control's menu row is back to the original wording.
rows.correction: The behaviour is exactly as claimed for a toplevel remount that rebinds the viewport role (client_layout_mode change, root 548 -> 164), but one of the three triggers they list is wrong: a window resize that does not change the root (fixed mode, 765x503 -> 1200x800) does not rebind the viewport and does not revert the label. I could not exercise the "provided-gameframe switch" trigger because GF_MATRIX_WIDGET_DEMO=1 runs the probe with TORIRS_WIDGET_DEMO=only and no frame plugin. Scope note for severity: widget-demo is the probe registered only under TORIRS_WIDGET_DEMO, not a shipped plugin, and the fault is in the demo's own on-config/BOUND split (src/plugin/plugins/widget_demo.c:98-103 vs :124-134), not in the widget/config API. The second half of their finding (the silent early return at :129 when state->control is not yet created) is a code reading only; I did not produce a run where it is user-visible.

result.claim: After a toplevel remount the widget-demo "rearm" setting stops reaching the tree: the config still reads true (and is on disk) but the owned control's menu row is back to the original wording, because the viewport BOUND branch recreates the control and arms it with the ORIGINAL label without re-reading "rearm".
result.what_i_ran:
Four of my own m01 OSRS239 captures (GF_MATRIX_WIDGET_DEMO=1, TORIRS_MINIMENU_DEBUG=1), each isolating one variable, all right-clicking the owned control at 40,62 (control bounds 16,60 180x16 fixed / 12,56 after remount):
A (positive control) TORIRS_SIM_PLUGIN_CONFIG="450,widget-demo,rearm,1", click 600 — no remount.
B (repro) same rearm at 450, plus TORIRS_SIM_CMD="500,layout 2" (root 548 -> 164), click 600, GF_MATRIX_EXPECT_ROOT=164.
C (counter-case for their "resize" trigger) rearm at 450, TORIRS_SIM_RESIZE="500,1200x800", click 600.
D (order reversed) layout 2 at 450, rearm at 550, click 630.
Then cropped each out.bmp to the menu region at 3x and read the image; checked plugin_prefs.ini and pixels.txt for each run.
result.what_i_saw:
A: log "WIDGET_DEMO_REARM result=0" then "minimenu: row[1] 'Re-armed: set public chat to friends' action=500008"; the pixels show that wording in the Choose Option box.
B: same REARM result=0 at line 1812, then at 1985-1987 "WIDGET_DEMO_UNBOUND / WIDGET_DEMO api=3 before=7,7 190x261 after=-5,7 / WIDGET_DEMO_OP_BOUNDS armed=0 x=12 y=56 w=180 h=16" — the viewport rebind recreated the control — and the right-click afterwards reports "minimenu: row[1] 'Set public chat to friends'". Same click coordinate, same session, only the remount differs, so the row is a real revert and not a missed hit. D: remount first, rearm second — REARM result=0 lands after the rebind and the row reads "Re-armed: ..." again, so the engine's config delivery path is healthy; it is purely the BOUND branch not re-reading the key.

rows.behaviour: The obvious way to run just the demo, TORIRS_PLUGIN_ONLY=widget-demo (what GF_MATRIX_PLUGIN=widget-demo exports), starts a client with ZERO plugins and says nothing.
rows.correction: What is true is only the residual: PluginRegistry_RegisterAll returns without registering or logging anything when TORIRS_PLUGIN_ONLY names an id outside PLUGIN_TABLE, so a person invoking the binary by hand with a typo'd id gets no message from the client. What is false is everything the "major" rating rests on. There is no broken way to run the demo -- GF_MATRIX_WIDGET_DEMO=1 registers widget-demo and passes its gates. The selector is not broken -- a real id registers and passes. And the failure is not silent through the harness, which is the only path that sets TORIRS_PLUGIN_ONLY at all: it always pairs the export with --plugin-id, so the very command in the finding printed selected_plugin_running=FAIL and exited 1. The defect is a missing client-side diagnostic (arguably an assert per CLAUDE.md) with no user-visible misbehaviour and no lost capability: minor, not major.

rows.correction: No correction to the behaviour; one precision worth recording. The settings panel is not an entry point — app_plugin_choices_add/app_plugin_choice_index only ever emit a declared choice, so a user clicking the dropdown cannot reach this. The two reachable entry points are exactly the ones the claim names: a plugin calling api.config.set with an undeclared string, and the plugin_prefs.ini text file (which the host writes and re-reads, and which I observed carrying style=classic after the run). Neither the set path nor the load path consults ToriRS_ConfigItem.choices anywhere in src/plugin.

rows.behaviour: SUSPICION (map: 'Hidden metrics are still positioned, landing exactly on top of the next visible line'). Turning a metric off should leave nothing behind.
rows.correction: What is true: layout_labels() does set_position/set_size before the `if api.config[metric.visible]` guard, so a disabled metric's owned text node keeps a 132x15 box at the next visible row and is never hidden or removed. What is NOT true is every consequence claimed. (a) Nothing is left behind on screen — update_text() sets the disabled label to "" (len=0), and I measured zero ink of the plugin's colour inside the leftover node's rectangle. (b) It is not a click target and does not become one by stacking: an owned node produces a minimenu row only when it carries an op serial, this plugin declares none, and a right-click inside the leftover box is byte-identical to the same click with all plugins off. (c) The "stacked over the next visible line" framing is the harmless half of the shape: when a leading metric is off the leftover rect is exactly a SUBSET of a visible line's rect, so it can never cover anything the visible line does not; the only rectangle it holds alone is when a trailing metric is off, where it is on top of nothing at all. The residue is dead code hygiene — a latent hazard if owned text nodes ever gain a background, border or hit box — with no present user-visible or input-visible effect.

result.claim: performance_display.lua positions/sizes every metric before the visibility guard, so a disabled metric keeps a real 132x15 owned text node (hidden=0) stacked exactly on the next visible row's rectangle — two owned nodes sharing one rectangle, which become stacked click targets over the scene.

(a) Nothing is left behind on screen — update_text() sets the disabled label to "" (len=0), and I measured zero ink of the plugin's colour inside the leftover node's rectangle. (b) It is not a click target and does not become one by stacking: an owned node produces a minimenu row only when it carries an op serial, this plugin declares none, and a right-click inside the leftover box is byte-identical to the same click with all plugins off. (c) The "stacked over the next visible line" framing is the harmless half of the shape: when a leading metric is off the leftover rect is exactly a SUBSET of a visible line's rect, so it can never cover anything the visible line does not; the only rectangle it holds alone is when a trailing metric is off, where it is on top of nothing at all. The residue is dead code hygiene — a latent hazard if owned text nodes ever gain a background, border or hit box — with no present user-visible or input-visible effect.
